steps.title: Burst-wise FCS on a demonstration data set
steps.text:
This tool correlates the photons inside each single-molecule burst separately, so the curves are not diluted by the empty time between bursts.

The tour works on a small data set the tool writes itself: eight bursts on two detectors, drawn from a seeded generator (nothing here is a measurement). Press Example to add it.

steps.title: The input and the channel pairs
steps.text: The table of burst files now lists the burst table of the demonstration data, ticked. Below it are the channel pairs: one auto-correlation per detector (ACF_0, ACF_1) and their cross-correlation (cross_01). A pair is two lists of routing channels, optionally gated in micro time; double-click a cell to edit it.

steps.title: Run the correlation
steps.text: Press Run FCS. Every ticked burst is correlated for every ticked pair (8 bursts x 3 pairs = 24 curves) with the multi-tau settings of the Settings tab.

steps.title: Look at one burst
steps.text: The Curves list shows every curve with its fitted diffusion time. Click a row to show that burst: the white line is the correlation, the red line its single-component diffusion fit. The filter box above the list narrows it by file or pair name.

steps.title: Choose the fit
steps.text: On the Settings tab the Mode chooses the fit: None shows the raw curves, Simple fits one diffusing species with a triplet, MaxEnt inverts the curve into a distribution of diffusion times. Click MaxEnt, then press Run FCS again to see the distribution in the lower plot.

steps.title: Set the fit window
steps.text: The two blue vertical lines on the correlation plot are the window the fit uses (t_min and t_max on the Settings tab). Short lags of a single burst are shot noise: drag the left line to the right to leave them out, then run again.

steps.title: Your own data
steps.text: Add your burst tables with Files... (BUR or BST), Folder... (an analysis folder) or Database..., or drop them on the window. On the Detector setup tab the shared detector editor defines the channels; Use setup for pairs turns a setup into channel pairs. Export curves... saves the curves and fits as JSON.
